title: fix(cli): show why a command failed when the config cannot be read
body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/196815

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when the config file cannot be read, commands such as `openclaw status` say only "The CLI command failed." and send the user to `openclaw doctor`, which fails the same way, instead of naming the file that could not be read.

## User Impact

User impact: a user with an unreadable config now sees why the command failed:

```text
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] Reason: Config could not be read at /home/user/.openclaw/openclaw.json:
- <root>: Failed to read include file: missing.json (resolved: /home/user/.openclaw/missing.json)
```

The circular "run `openclaw doctor`" line is no longer printed for this failure, since Doctor cannot read the file either.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before a command runs, the CLI reads the config to choose the storage engine. When that read fails, the error is thrown without being printed, and the root failure output only showed a reason for invalid configs and a few named commands, so the read error was dropped. The root failure output now treats a config read failure the way it already treats state-database refusals: it prints the title and the redacted reason, without the Doctor line. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/158671 separated read failures from invalid configs and removed Doctor advice for them on the paths it touched; this is the root path it did not reach.

Behavior to know:

- Only errors with code `CONFIG_READ_FAILED` change. Invalid configs, state-database refusals and every other failure keep their current output.
- The reason goes through the same redaction as other reasons; nested causes and stacks stay behind `OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1`.
- `--json` failure output is unchanged.
- `openclaw config validate`, setup and bare `openclaw` are not changed here; https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166573 (open) owns their read-failure wording, and this change does not touch its files.

Docs: `docs/cli/index.md` gains one line under failure output.

## Evidence

Tested at c8eae97758c47952377cb1995b3fb081b1f8b59a (baseline 080ed32005690b75b9d6860b0582a3f335290e94).

Before/After at the CLI boundary: a before/after harness built both sides from source and ran the same steps in fresh isolated homes. Each side wrote a config whose only content is `{"$include":"missing.json"}` and then ran `openclaw status`, `openclaw agents list` and `openclaw doctor --non-interactive`. All three exit 1 on both sides; stdout is identical. Stderr, with the per-side home path normalized:

```diff
 [openclaw] The CLI command failed.
-[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
+[openclaw] Reason: Config could not be read at <openclaw-home>/.openclaw/openclaw.json:
+- <root>: Failed to read include file: missing.json (resolved: <openclaw-home>/.openclaw/missing.json)
```

The same difference appears for all three commands. The expectation "stderr names the read error" is not met before and is met after for each of them.

Regression test: a `createConfigReadError` row in the existing "keeps actionable refusal details without leaking diagnostics" table of `src/cli/failure-output.test.ts`. It expects the read error as the reason, no Doctor line, and no leaked token, nested cause or stack. It fails on the baseline (the reason line is missing) and passes at the head; the other 20 tests in the file pass on both.

Checks at the head:

- `pnpm test src/cli/failure-output.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 21 passed.
- Typecheck of `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.config-cli.json`: clean.
- oxfmt: clean. `scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts`: `Test lines OK`.
- oxlint did not run locally (the local install lacked a lint plugin dependency); CI runs it.

Local review: autoreview (Codex gpt-6.1-sol, medium), base 080ed32005690b75b9d6860b0582a3f335290e94 to head c8eae97758c47952377cb1995b3fb081b1f8b59a, priority P0–P1: scoped-clean, no remaining findings.

Simplification pass: the smallest complete fix is one branch at the existing root failure printer, which already decides which reasons are shown. Fixing it at the throw site would print the error twice. Against the merge base, production code is +5/−1 (a four-line branch and the import), test code +6/−1 (one table row and the import), and docs +1. Nothing was removed because no duplicate path exists.

| Test file | Added cost |
| --- | --- |
| `src/cli/failure-output.test.ts` | one row in an existing `it.each` table; `pnpm test src/cli/failure-output.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 57.5 s wall locally, almost all of it worker startup; the new row adds no measurable CI seconds |

Not covered:

- Unreadable files for other reasons (permissions, a failed SQLite snapshot read) go through the same `CONFIG_READ_FAILED` error, but only the missing include was run end to end.
- `openclaw models list` and other commands that select the storage engine take the same path but were not run end to end.
- Commands that read the config themselves after engine selection (`config validate`, setup, bare `openclaw`) keep their own output; see https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166573.
